utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 282.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we show the witness Exhibit 239, please. Can you please scroll the document down for the witness to look at the document? It's an order by General Delic, and it appears that you drafted this document. It bears your initials.

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct, I did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: The document relates to the action plan for Trebevic-3?

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Now, again I would like you to look at paragraph numbered 5. Do you agree that this act -- please look at paragraph numbered 5: "In case it happens that persons resist arrest, if they offer resistance, use all means available, including weapons"?

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Do you agree that with this order, General Delic ordered weapons to be used in the same way that he ordered that in the other -- the previous order on Trebevic-2 in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: In the same way?

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: In other words, the units in the field received an order that in fighting with -- or in their fight against crime, they should use weapons in order that appropriate disciplinary and criminal proceedings could be instituted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I just want the witness to look here at paragraph 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at paragraph numbered 6 of this document, where it says: "In the area of responsibility of the corps in which the Trebevic-3 action is carried out, determine certain facilities, as collection centres, with maximum security, immediately conduct screening and premature investigations in order to conduct disciplinary and criminal procedures." In other words, I understand that General provided for the arrest of a large number of persons, and even for the setting up of a collections centre where triage could be performed immediately and investigations conducted, and where the criminals could be separated from those who were not criminals.

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And you know this order was ordered and that it was sent to all the corps of the Bosnia-Herzegovina Army; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: Yes, this should have been dispatched to all of the corps, and you can see that from this particular paragraph that it should have been dispatched to all the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you very much. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just have a few questions for the witness. Witness. I do expect that I will probably go past the 1.45 time limit, though. If the witness could be shown Exhibit 271.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you say that again, Mr. Menon?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Exhibit number 271.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to remind you, while we're waiting for the exhibit, that there is another trial after this, so we will have to stop at quarter to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Mr. Softic, do you -- can you tell me who this document was addressed to, if anybody?

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: The document is written in such a way in which I would not draft it. From the heading, you would immediately need to see whom the document is addressed; whereas, in this document you can only see in the actual text that the document is being sent to the 3rd Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can you point out where you see that particular text, that it's being sent to the 3rd Corps Command?

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: It states at the top authorisation, authorising Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin, member of the 3rd Corps Command, only on the basis of the fact that Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin was a member of the 3rd Corps Command is it obvious to me that the document was being sent to the 3rd Corps Command. But I don't see that it was actually sent to that Command. The document should have me, perhaps, as the person sending it from the Cabinet, and also it should state the person to whom the document is addressed, the Staff of the Command, saying that the document is being dispatched to the 3rd Corps Command, but we don't have that, we don't see that. Only on the basis of the actual contents, the text, do we see that the document should have been sent to the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I were to say that the document entitles Mr. Mahmuljin to carry out certain activities? Is that apparent to you from the first statement in the document?

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: You can see that from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: In that case, would it be possible that this document would have been handed to Mr. Mahmuljin, based upon your experience working in the Cabinet?

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: If the document was to have any kind of official marking based on which Mahmuljin would act, it had to go through a specific procedure. Everything else is questionable. If the document was dispatched without the proper protocol, without it being entered into the protocol at the 3rd Corps, it would throw doubt on the whole document. I would never receive such a document. Had the document been sent to me and someone had added a remark in handwriting that this is for such-and-such a person, I would not have received such a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Mr. Softic, I'm simply -- I'm not asking you whether the document was dispatched. I'm simply asking you, based upon the content, based upon that first sentence, and since you agree that the document entitles Mr. Mahmuljin to carry out certain activities, whether it's possible that it was handed to him.

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: I couldn't say, I really couldn't say. On the basis of my experience, I couldn't do it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And the stamp which appears on the document, is that familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: Yes, the stamp is familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And why is it familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: Because of the writing on the stamp and the size. Well, the size varied, but not the content.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And when you say "the size varied, but not the content," does that mean that similar stamps appeared on other documents that originated from the Cabinet?

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: Documents that were signed by the Commander had one stamp. I don't know about others.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: Documents signed by the Commander had one stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I just have one final question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Is this the stamp that those documents would have?

utterances.speaker: MURAT SOFTIC
utterances.text: I think that it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll continue tomorrow, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The case now stands adjourned to tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning in Courtroom II, this same courtroom here. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 29th day of August, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
